question: In zod 4 (github.com/colinhacks/zod, the `zod` package), when the input is `undefined`, how does the behavior of `.prefault(x)` differ from `.default(x)` with respect to whether the substituted value `x` is run through the schema's own parsing/validation? Explain the difference in outcome, not just that both exist.
critical_facts: explains that .default(x) short-circuits: on undefined input it returns the default value immediately WITHOUT running it through the inner schema's validation/transforms
explains that .prefault(x) substitutes x as the input and THEN runs it through the inner schema (so validation and transforms DO apply to the prefault value)
the distinguishing point is that prefault passes the value through the validator while default does not
material_errors: claims .default() runs the default value through the schema's validation/transforms (it does not — it returns immediately)
claims .prefault() and .default() are identical, or reverses which one validates the substituted value
cites the legacy v3 `.default()` implementation (packages/zod/src/v3/...) as the zod 4 answer
evidence: packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:3648-3653 — $ZodDefault forward: `payload.value = def.defaultValue; ... return payload;` with comment "It doesn't pass the default value into the validator"
packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:3711-3717 — $ZodPrefault forward: on undefined `payload.value = def.defaultValue;` then `return def.innerType._zod.run(payload, ctx);` (runs through innerType)
